meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have to tell me.
Did you chop the carrots?
Why do you not wear it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты опять намекаешь, что я толстый?
examples.trans: Are you hinting again that I am fat?

examples.text: Нет, я просто говорю, что был стройный.
examples.trans: No, I am just saying that you were slim.
What is the matter, Lyova? Easy.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cognac' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Kostyan, did you break the cognac?

examples.text: Там был коньяк, и он дешёвый был.
examples.trans: There was cognac there, and it was cheap.

examples.text: Слушай, ты не мог сказать, что Пригожин коньяк разбил?
examples.trans: Listen, could you not say that Prigozhin broke the cognac?

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke', paired with 'разбивать'.

examples.trans: Kostyan, did you break the cognac?
Did you break something?

examples.text: Я? Нет, я ничего не разбивал.
examples.trans: Me? No, I did not break anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just as I assumed.
And why do I not know?
I do not owe you anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты что, не видел, что я здесь стою?
examples.trans: Did you not see that I am standing here?
I am simply tidying up here.
Sign right here, please.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is just a crack!

examples.text: Нет, я просто говорю, что был стройный.
examples.trans: No, I am just saying that you were slim.
I just wanted to check.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'бираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'clean up, tidy up'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и прибираться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and clean up on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют прибираться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to clean up.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
You have an incomplete rib fracture.
Just as I assumed.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, that is what it is.
It is just a crack!

examples.text: Я изменился, я сейчас это докажу.
examples.trans: I have changed, I will prove it right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well there, something like that.
So here is the deal.
What is the matter, Lyova? Easy.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('children's, childish').

examples.trans: A baby crib.
What childish words.
This is the children's room.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'baby crib, cot' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A baby crib.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть кроватка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always baby crib.

meanings.en: to sign (a receipt, register, or document)
meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'писаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sign', paired with 'расписываться'.

examples.trans: Here, you need to sign the payment sheet.
Sign here, please.

examples.text: Это ваш аванс. Вот в ведомости расписаться надо.
examples.trans: This is your advance. Here, you need to sign the payment sheet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Sit down right here and do not strain yourself.
Well there, something like that.

examples.text: Вот что ты ей хочешь сказать?
examples.trans: Now what do you want to say to her?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: That is outrageous! Lyova, forgive me, please.
Sign right here, please.
A coffee, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: That is outrageous! Lyova, forgive me, please.
Forgive me, I mixed everything up.
Forgive me for not believing you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'путать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'mixed up', paired with 'путать'.

examples.trans: Forgive me, I mixed everything up.
Champagne for lovers? Apparently they mixed it up.
Don't mix it up!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Заодно объясню, почему всё так вышло.
examples.trans: At the same time I will explain why it all happened this way.
Forgive me, I mixed everything up.

examples.text: Спасибо, Соломон Иванович. Теперь всё можно!
examples.trans: Thank you, Solomon Ivanovich. Now everything is allowed!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'instead of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Instead of the home address I wrote the work one.

examples.text: Знаешь, я очень рада, что мы вместе.
examples.trans: You know, I am very glad that we are together.
Go instead of me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'машний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('house').

examples.trans: Instead of the home address I wrote the work one.
This is house arrest.
Where is the homework?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'address' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Instead of the home address I wrote the work one.
Alright, give me your address.
Write me your address.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'indicated, wrote down'.

examples.trans: Instead of the home address I wrote the work one.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и указать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and indicated on time.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working').

examples.trans: Instead of the home address I wrote the work one.
That means thousands of jobs.
A working day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.
You have an incomplete rib fracture.
You said it was a crack.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледующий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('next').

examples.trans: Next time you will be more careful.
Don't be late next time.

examples.text: А ты в следующий раз на мои деньги не рассчитывай. И всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Well, next time don't count on my money. And everything will be fine.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шеф, а вы как раз вовремя.
examples.trans: Chef, you are right on time.

examples.text: Она со мной даже разговаривать не хочет.
examples.trans: She does not even want to talk to me.
Kostyan, did you break the cognac?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will'.

examples.trans: I wanted to look like you.
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Next time you will be more careful.
Read everything carefully!
Listen to the teacher attentively.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Может, это она на вас так влияет?
examples.trans: Maybe she is influencing you like that?
Maybe she is the one who decided?
Maybe I can pay you extra?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You said it was a crack.

examples.text: Вы же знаете, кто у вас будет?
examples.trans: Do you know who you are having?
She is working her first day today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'платить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will pay extra'.

related.gloss: not to will pay extra (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и доплатить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will pay extra on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют доплатить.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to will pay extra.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: Давай я помогу. Хочешь пригласить её на свидание?
examples.trans: Let me help. Do you want to invite her on a date?
Vika, let me drive it over.
Let me help you, huh?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will drop off, deliver'.

related.gloss: not to will drop off (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Vika, let me drive it over.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и завезти вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will drop off on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'грузить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will load', paired with 'загружать'.

examples.trans: We loaded the things into the car.

examples.text: Да, все вещи уже загрузили в багажник.
examples.trans: Yes, all things have already been loaded into the trunk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Загружу машину, а потом помогу поднять.
examples.trans: I will load the car and then help carry it up.
Is this our car now?
Which car did you come in?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.

examples.text: Загружу машину, а потом помогу поднять.
examples.trans: I will load the car and then help carry it up.

examples.text: Ладно, пачкай тарелки, потом иди мой.
examples.trans: Alright, dirty the plates, then go wash them.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Давай я помогу. Хочешь пригласить её на свидание?
examples.trans: Let me help. Do you want to invite her on a date?

examples.text: Загружу машину, а потом помогу поднять.
examples.trans: I will load the car and then help carry it up.
Let me help you, huh?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to lift', paired with 'поднимать'.

examples.text: Загружу машину, а потом помогу поднять.
examples.trans: I will load the car and then help carry it up.
I'll rally people!
Raise your hand.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have an incomplete rib fracture.
No. Stop it!
And why do I not know?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Шеф, а что вы решили, что надо худеть?
examples.trans: Chef, why did you decide that you need to lose weight?

examples.text: Не надо. Костя, чем это пахнет?
examples.trans: No need. Kostya, what is that smell?

examples.text: Видишь, как опасно надо мной шутить!
examples.trans: See how dangerous it is to joke with me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'than', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And why do I not know?
Chef, why do you need that?

examples.text: Заодно объясню, почему всё так вышло.
examples.trans: At the same time I will explain why it all happened this way.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to smell (give off a smell)'.

examples.trans: It smells bad here.
The coffee smells good.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.
